titulo_en: Mustn't, don't have to and had to

titulo_es.@es: distinguir prohibición, falta de necesidad y obligación pasada
titulo_es.@en: to distinguish prohibition, lack of need and past obligation

texto.@es: **Mustn't + verbo base** significa que algo está prohibido: **You mustn't run here.** **Don't/doesn't have to + verbo base** significa que no es necesario hacerlo; puede hacerse, pero no es obligatorio.
texto.@en: **Mustn't + verbo base** means something is prohibited: **You mustn't run here.** **Don't/doesn't have to + verbo base** means that it is not necessary to do so; it can be done, but it is not mandatory.

texto.@es: Usa **had to + verbo base** para una obligación pasada. Usa **didn't have to + verbo base** cuando no era necesario hacerlo. Después de **didn't**, escribe **have**, no **had**. **Didn't have to** no indica por sí solo si la persona finalmente lo hizo.
texto.@en: Use **had to + verbo base** for a past obligation. Use **didn't have to + verbo base** when it was not necessary. After **didn't**, write **have**, not **had**. **Didn't have to** does not indicate by itself whether the person finally did.

frases.en: We didn't have to bring cash because the lockers were free.
